1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O d6.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Improved Steinitz Defence
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O d6.background: Once a frequent alternative to 4...Nxe4; Emanuel Lasker played it twice in the 1908 World Championship match.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O d6 5.d.strategy: Opens the centre at once, putting two attackers on e5 while Black's ...d6 has spent a tempo on defence. White gets space and easy development, and Black has to hold e5 rather than counterattack.
Blocks the diagonal from b5 to the king, so the c6 knight is no longer pinned and can capture on d4 while e5 stays defended. A solid, compact set-up that completes development and prepares to castle.

Retreats the knight so that e5 gets another defender and the pawn chain holds without any exchange. The price is a clumsy set-up: the knight blocks the c8-bishop, and White gets the space and the choice of plan.
